procedural_history.impugned_order: Order dated 30.04.2014 of the High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan at Jaipur in S. B. Cr. Revision Petition No. 341 of 2014.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The appellant preferred a revision petition against an order (likely from the Magistrate Court). The High Court dismissed the revision petition in limine (at the threshold) based on the absence of sanction and the fact that the revision petition was directed against an interlocutory order.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant filed a Special Leave Petition (SLP) challenging the High Court's order. The Supreme Court issued notice to the respondents (except respondent No. 4). Respondent No. 1 sought deletion from the array of parties. The matter was referred to a larger bench along with SLP (CRL.) No. 5838/2014.

directions: The matter is referred to a larger Bench along with SLP (CRL.) No.5838/2014 in terms of the judgment passed today.

issue.issue_text: Whether the matter should be referred to a larger Bench for consideration.

facts: The case involves the question of whether a Magistrate can order an investigation under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C.).
law: The central legal issue is whether a direction for investigation under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. can be issued without prior sanction, particularly in cases involving offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act (P.C. Act).
application: The Court identified this issue as a "larger question" and a "conundrum" arising from the interplay between the P.C. Act and the Cr.P.C.
The Court found that this significant legal controversy needed to be settled authoritatively.
reasoning.conclusion: Due to the importance and complexity of the legal question regarding the necessity of prior sanction, the Court concluded that the matter should be referred to a larger Bench for consideration and settlement.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the matter should be referred to a larger Bench for consideration.

statutes.section: A provision, whose section number is not specified, stating: '(a) no finding, sentence or order passed by a special Judge shall be reversed or altered by a court in appeal, confirmation or revision on the ground of the absence of, or any error, omission or irregularity in, the sanction required under sub-section (1), unless in the opinion of that court, a failure of justice has in fact been occasioned thereby;'

ratio_decidendi.ratio: No binding legal rule was established on the substantive legal question, as the court referred the matter to a larger Bench for an authoritative pronouncement.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court found that despite a "catena of judgments" on the issue, a "different path has been traversed in two judgments of this Court where the offences alleged are under the P.C. Act read with the I.P.C.", creating a conflict that requires resolution by a larger bench.
legal_tests_applied: The judicial principle that when there are conflicting judgments from benches of coordinate strength on a point of law, the matter should be referred to a larger bench to settle the legal position.
policy_considerations: The need to resolve conflicting precedents from the same court to ensure consistency, legal certainty, and the uniform application of law.
